question: What is exact universal message capacity under behavior preservation and operational closure?
closest_work_delta: Watermark literature supplies constructions and attack models; this asks the semantic existence question jointly.
claim: Capacity is min_C |C/J|, with matching construction and impossibility.
minimum_decisive_evidence: Complete iff proof and finite exhaustive checker.
falsifier: Any finite counterexample to either direction.
generality: Arbitrary program set and equivalence contracts.
reason: Sharp exact boundary with direct PL semantics consequence.

question: What replaces local quotient counts when operational classes cross behavior classes?
closest_work_delta: Adds a global consistency layer absent from local counting arguments.
claim: Feasibility iff the quotient hypergraph has a polychromatic message coloring.
mechanism: Global decoder labels quotient cells; each behavior class must contain every label.
minimum_decisive_evidence: Iff proof and minimal odd-cycle counterexample.
falsifier: Mismatch between feasible schemes and colorings.
generality: Arbitrary finite/infinite underlying program sets; finite message alphabet.
reason: Necessary to avoid a hidden refinement assumption.

question: Does full semantic observation permit arbitrary behavior-preserving watermark insertion?
closest_work_delta: Separates recognition of behavior from insertion of owner-selected information.
claim: Every behavior class has one operational cell and zero insertable bits.
falsifier: Two differently decoded behavior-equivalent outputs under a semantics-only decoder.
reason: Strong consequence but insufficient alone for journal depth.

question: How do detector abstractions and multiple attack families compose?
closest_work_delta: Attack resilience is usually assessed family by family.
assumptions: Decoded message equality is required along every detector/attack edge.
claim: All requirements compose through equivalence closure; capacity is monotone under stronger closure.
minimum_decisive_evidence: Factor lemma, monotonicity law, non-independent-accounting example.
falsifier: Robust decoder varying within generated closure.
generality: Any family of binary operational relations.
reason: Provides the calculus that gives the theorem operational meaning.

question: Which predicates are robustly recognizable and which can be universally toggled?
closest_work_delta: Existing semantic watermarking work often conflates recognizing a property with inserting a selected bit.
claim: Robust predicates are J-saturated; universal toggling also requires both truth values in every behavior class.
mechanism: Quotient Boolean algebra and two-representative choice.
minimum_decisive_evidence: Two iff theorems and contrasting examples.
falsifier: Robust non-saturated predicate or toggle scheme in a monochromatic behavior class.
reason: Necessary conceptual separation supporting the capacity theorem.

question: When is a semantic predicate recognizable from finite observational evidence?
closest_work_delta: Connects contextual profiles to open/clopen finite-certificate structure.
assumptions: Discrete outcomes and product topology; compactness for uniformity.
claim: Positive finite evidence iff open; two-sided iff clopen; compact clopen sets depend on one finite context set.
minimum_decisive_evidence: Complete elementary proofs and boundary examples.
falsifier: Open set lacking pointwise finite certificate or compact clopen set lacking finite dependence.

question: Can a practical source-to-source transformer realize the capacity bound?
closest_work_delta: Would move from existence to construction.
assumptions: Concrete language, equivalence checker, benchmark corpus, attack implementations.
claim: Algorithm realizes marks with measured robustness.
falsifier: Failure to preserve behavior or survive attacks.
cost: High and risks duplicating a concrete channel project.
reason: Outside independence boundary and cannot be decisive without a concrete evaluation program.

question: Can the calculus be mechanized in a proof assistant?
closest_work_delta: Would strengthen proof assurance rather than alter the result.
assumptions: Library support for quotients, choice, topology, and finite hypergraphs.
claim: Machine-checked correspondence for all main statements.
falsifier: Core theorem cannot be represented without changing assumptions.
generality: Same as paper modulo foundational choices.
reason: Human proofs and independent finite checker already close the central evidence contract.
